title: Chourio walk-off carries Brewers to 2-0 NLDS lead over Padres on October 4
dek: Jackson Chourio delivered a two-out, two-strike single in the bottom of the ninth inning on October 4 to give Milwaukee a 4-3 walk-off victory over San Diego in Game 2 of the NLDS. The Brewers extended their series lead to 2-0 and moved one win away from advancing. It marked the first last-inning comeback in franchise postseason history that began with Milwaukee trailing.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Chourio's two-out, two-strike single in the ninth inning scored Christian Yelich and Sal Frelick to give the Brewers a 4-3 walk-off win and a 2-0 NLDS series lead.
bottom_line: Milwaukee needs one more victory to reach the next round and will look to close out the series in San Diego starting October 6. The Padres must win both remaining games at home to force a Game 5 back in Milwaukee.
body: Jackson Chourio delivered a two-out, two-strike single in the bottom of the ninth inning to lift the Milwaukee Brewers past the San Diego Padres 4-3 on October 4, extending the Brewers' NLDS series lead to 2-0. The hit scored Christian Yelich and Sal Frelick and sent a sellout crowd of 41,683 at American Family Field into celebration.

The moment marked the first last-inning comeback in Brewers postseason history that began with Milwaukee trailing, according to MLB.com. It was the franchise's third postseason walk-off win overall. Mason Miller, the Padres' elite closer, allowed the single after Milwaukee had entered the ninth inning trailing 3-2.

Yelich worked a walk and stole second base to start the ninth-inning sequence. Frelick came back from a 1-2 count to walk, loading the bases with two outs. Gary Sánchez then laid off a 103.3 mph fastball just below the zone before walking on a slider to bring up Chourio, who was facing his second high-leverage situation of the game. Chourio had grounded out with the bases loaded in the seventh inning two innings earlier, per MLB.com's reporting.

Chourio worked the count to 1-2 before connecting for the six-pitch single. At 22 years old, Chourio is Milwaukee's all-time leader in postseason home runs, per the reporting. During the regular season, he set career highs in batting average (.291), on-base percentage (.351), and slugging percentage (.487) and authored his third straight 20-20 campaign to begin his career, matching a feat accomplished only by Julio Rodríguez and Bobby Witt Jr., according to MLB.com.

Milwaukee trailed after a wild pitch by Logan Henderson in the first inning, and the Brewers committed three errors matching their season high. The team had finished the regular season with 103 wins and secured their fourth straight division title on the back of Chourio's two-run tying homer in the ninth inning of a September 8 comeback win over the Cubs that was part of a three-game sweep. Garrett Mitchell said of this Brewers team that "we're in it until the 27th out," per MLB.com's account.
The Brewers head to San Diego for Games 3 and 4 needing one win to advance. The series returns to the Padres' home field for the next two contests.
